In 897, a pope put a dead pope on trial.
Pope Formosus had been dead for nine months. A later pope, Stephen the Sixth, hated him.
So Stephen had him dug up, dressed in his papal robes, and propped up on a throne.
A young deacon stood next to the corpse, to answer the questions for him.
Stephen screamed accusations at the body. The body said nothing.
His decisions were canceled. They cut off the three fingers he used to give blessings, and threw him into the River Tiber.
Not long after, the basilica where the trial was held collapsed.
People saw it as a sign. Rome turned against Stephen.
Within months, he was thrown in prison, and strangled.
A monk pulled Formosus out of the river, and he was buried again, in Saint Peter's.
And a later pope made it official. No more putting dead people on trial.
